judge_assessment.explanation: I performed all twelve divisions and every quotient and remainder in the key is right: x+5; x+3+3/(x+2); x^2-x-6; 2x^2-3x+4-8/(x+3) with p(-3) = -8; x^2+2x+4; 3x^2+x-2; 2x^2-2x+7-10/(x+1) with p(-1) = -10; x^2+2x-4+(2x-1)/(x^2+1); x^3+2x^2-x-2; 3x^2+x+2-2/(x-1) with the multiply-back rebuilding 3x^3-2x^2+x-4; 2x^2-x-3+(-x-2)/(x^2-x+1); and x^3-4x^2+x+6 = (x-3)(x-2)(x+1). I also agree with the visual_and_print_quality 3: six pages for twelve short divisions is two problems per page, and the gate log shows 109.6cm of declared content against an ideal of five pages. One thing the judge did not look at is the Quick Answers bank, where the renderer reorders the authored form: row 8 prints "x^2 + 2x + (2x-1)/(x^2+1) - 4" and row 11 prints "2x^2 - x + (-x-2)/(x^2-x+1) - 3", pushing the quotient's constant term past the fraction on a sheet whose directions require the answer "as quotient + remainder over divisor". The values are correct; the printed form is not the taught one.

strengths_to_preserve: This packet is the batch's counter-example on verification coverage: every multi-part request has its own entry. Problem 4 declares both the quotient and the remainder-theorem check p(-3) = -8, problem 10 declares both the quotient and an `expand` entry that rebuilds 3x^3-2x^2+x-4 from (x-1)(3x^2+x+2)-2, and problem 12 declares both the quotient and the complete factorisation.

The ramp is deliberately built on the two ways long division fails: missing powers (problems 5, 7, 9, 11) and stopping at the wrong degree (problem 8's quadratic divisor, whose stem says the division stops as soon as what is left has degree below 2).

Problems 4 and 7 pair each division with the substitution check at the divisor's zero, and each carries a declared trap for substituting +3 or +1 instead (70 and 4), so the remainder theorem is taught as a check the student can run alone.

The study guide's two worked examples are re-parameterisations of the worksheet's own hazards (a linear divisor with a negative remainder, then a dividend missing its square term), and each try-it answer is verified.

root_causes.description: render_quick_answers._fmt sympifies a string `expected` with the evaluating parser, so SymPy's canonical ordering replaces the authored quotient + remainder/divisor arrangement in the delivered bank.
evidence: verify.json id 11 declares "2*x**2 - x - 3 + (-x - 2)/(x**2 - x + 1)"; answer_key.pdf prints the -3 after the fraction.
scripts/render_quick_answers.py::_fmt calls sympy.latex(sympy.sympify(v)) with no evaluate=False.

root_causes.description: Workspace was declared at the multi-step end of SKILL.md's defaults (7-10cm) for problems whose worked solutions run three or four lines, so the sheet consumed a page more than its own page-budget ideal.
evidence: gate_log.txt: "Page budget (ws, letter): 12 problems, 109.6cm of content ... ideal 5 page(s) ... 3 sheet(s) of paper double-sided", and the compile reports 6 pages.
verify.json declares workspace_cm of 9, 9, 9 and 10 for problems 8, 9, 10 and 11, whose key solutions are three to five lines each.
worksheet.pdf places exactly two problems on each of pages 1-6.

improvements.title: Preserve the authored algebraic form when rendering the Quick Answers bank
improvements.proposed_change: In scripts/render_quick_answers.py::_fmt, parse a string `expected` with sympy.sympify(v, evaluate=False) and fall back to the evaluating parse only if that raises, so SymPy cannot rewrite the form the author verified. Confirmed locally: sympy.latex(sympy.sympify('2*(x-3)*(x**2+3*x+9)')) yields '\left(2 x - 6\right) \left(x^{2} + 3 x + 9\right)', while the same call with evaluate=False yields '2 \left(x - 3\right) \left(x^{2} + 3 x + 9\right)'. Here rows 8 and 11 must print the quotient's constant term before the remainder fraction, matching the form the sheet's directions demand.
improvements.regression_test: tests/test_render_quick_answers.py gains a case rendering {"type": "factor", "expected": "2*(x-3)*(x**2+3*x+9)"}: the bank text must contain '2 \left(x - 3\right)' and must NOT contain '2 x - 6'. It fails against today's _fmt and passes after the change.
improvements.expected_impact: The at-a-glance grading column stops contradicting the worked key and stops modelling the exact error its worksheet targets.
improvements.risk: evaluate=False also stops harmless normalisation (a verified '4/2' would print as 4/2), so the change needs the numeric path left alone and the existing fixtures re-baselined.

improvements.title: Size declared workspace to the length of the worked solution
improvements.proposed_change: SKILL.md's "Work space defaults" reads as a floor of 5cm/8cm/10cm and is being applied at the top of the range for short procedural items. State that the workspace should hold the KEY's worked solution plus a line (a three-round long division or a two-step factorisation needs about 5cm, not 9-10cm), and have scripts/page_budget.py print an over-allocation notice when the declared content length exceeds the ideal page count by a full page. Here 12 short divisions declared 109.6cm and produced 6 pages against an ideal of 5.
improvements.regression_test: tests/test_page_budget.py gains a case: twelve problems each declaring 9cm whose keys are three lines long must emit the over-allocation notice and name the ideal page count; the same twelve at 5cm must not. No such notice exists today, so the assertion fails before the fix.
improvements.expected_impact: Recovers a sheet of paper per packet on procedural sets without ever shrinking the workspace on problems that genuinely need it.
improvements.risk: Workspace is the one thing SKILL.md says must never give; an advisory notice (not a hard gate) is essential so the guidance cannot be used to squeeze graph or proof problems.

case_summary: Complete and correct long-division fluency practice, and the batch's best example of a verify JSON that covers every printed deliverable - quotient, remainder-theorem check, multiply-back reconstruction and final factorisation each get their own entry. The two blemishes are presentational: the Quick Answers bank reorders two answers out of the quotient + remainder/divisor form the sheet insists on, and generous workspace defaults pushed twelve short problems onto six pages, which is what cost the visual and print dimension its point.
